Modern.tagline: Modern apothecary in the Materia Medica tradition.
Modern.brandNameRationale: Materia is the abbreviated Latin for Materia Medica — the canonical reference text of medicinal substances from Dioscorides (1st c.) through Culpeper (1653) and into modern pharmacognosy. Single-word brand placing the modern apothecary in the canonical-text tradition.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern herbalism has matured beyond the wellness aisle. The opening is for a brand that takes the Materia Medica register seriously — single herbs, named botanical sources, dosage in the traditional apothecary format.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Anima Mundi Herbals (animamundiherbals.com) holds the modern apothecary peer slot. Mountain Rose Herbs (mountainroseherbs.com) plays the trade-supply peer. Wooden Spoon Herbs (woodenspoonherbs.com) is the small-batch craft reference. We sit alongside Anima Mundi with sharper Materia Medica framing.
Modern.positioningStatement: A modern apothecary brand for single-herb tinctures and dried botanicals in the Materia Medica tradition.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 50. Reads ingredient lists carefully. Owns a small home apothecary, not a wellness stack.
behaviors: Buys single-herb tinctures by botanical name
Reads dosage in milliliters, not droppers
Subscribes to a single herbalist's seasonal restock

dos: Use the Latin binomial and the common name
List the part used (leaf, root, flower)
Publish the harvest location and method
donts: Blend herbs without naming each one

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark only — Materia set in a precise grotesk with a small herbal-press leaf silhouette as a hallmark on the bottle label.

typography.primary: GT America for the wordmark and labels
typography.secondary: Adobe Garamond for the long-form herb monograph
typography.rationale: GT America carries the modern apothecary register. Garamond is the canonical-text serif.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Hildegard von Bingen (1098–1179) — Benedictine abbess, composer, and the most influential medieval herbalist, author of Physica and Causae et Curae. The name places the brand directly in the 12th-century monastic apothecary tradition. Scholarly luxury register, fully out of copyright and unbranded.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury herbalism is dominated by French apothecary cosmetics. The opening is for a brand in the medieval-monastic-apothecary tradition — single-herb preparations, abbey-still register, documented sourcing from named gardens.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Santa Maria Novella (smnovella.com) holds the historic apothecary peer slot — Florentine 1612 tradition. Officina Profumo-Farmaceutica (smnovella.it) plays the same monastic-pharmacy peer. Buly 1803 (buly1803.com) is the historic-Parisian peer. We sit alongside Santa Maria Novella with a 12th-century monastic specificity.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A luxury monastic-tradition apothecary in the Hildegard Physica lineage, producing single-herb preparations and herbal cordials.

targetAudience.primary: 45 to 75. Buys at the heritage apothecary and the boutique pharmacy. Reads medieval and Renaissance herbal history.
behaviors: Buys at heritage apothecaries (Santa Maria Novella register)
Pays a premium for documented monastic-tradition preparations

dos: Use the Latin binomial and the medieval name

Luxury.logoDirection: A serif wordmark — Hildegard Apothecary set in a classical roman with a small embossed abbey-still mark above. The mark appears on the apothecary jar and the printed insert.

typography.primary: Caslon for the wordmark and signage
typography.secondary: Adobe Garamond for monographs and inserts
typography.rationale: Caslon carries the heritage apothecary register. Garamond handles the long-form herbal text.

Minimal.tagline: Minimal apothecary. One name, one part.
Minimal.brandNameRationale: Root names the part of the plant used in the most concentrated medicinal preparations across herbal traditions (valerian root, dandelion root, licorice root). Single-syllable, multi-meaning, trade-vocabulary anchor. Minimal apothecary brand with real herbalism roots.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimal herbalism is rare in a category drenched in wellness-stack copy. The opening is for a brand named on a single herbal-vocabulary word, with a stripped catalog of root preparations.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Wooden Spoon Herbs (woodenspoonherbs.com) holds the small-batch craft peer slot. Foster Botanica (fosterbotanica.com) plays the minimal craft peer. Anima Mundi Herbals (animamundiherbals.com) is the apothecary register reference. We sit further out — single-word brand, root-preparations-only catalog.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A minimal apothecary brand selling root tinctures and decoctions only.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 50. Owns three jars on the kitchen shelf. Wants single-herb preparations, not blends.
behaviors: Buys single-root tinctures one at a time
Reads the harvest week on the label

dos: Print the root species and harvest week

Minimal.logoDirection: Root set in a neutral grotesque, all lowercase, with a single tap-root silhouette beneath. No second mark.

typography.primary: ABC Diatype for the wordmark and body
typography.secondary: ABC Diatype Mono for harvest data and dosage
typography.rationale: One family. Mono for the data.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Botanica is the Latinate phrase for the botanical-medicine field — used across pharmacognosy, ethnobotany, and clinical botanical research. Partners names the B2B consultancy posture — clinical sourcing, regulatory affairs, and supply-chain due diligence for botanical-medicine manufacturers.
Corporate.industrySummary: Corporate herbalism is a serious B2B category — clinical-grade botanical sourcing, GMP-certified raw-material supply, and regulatory consulting for nutraceutical and pharmaceutical manufacturers. The opening is for a mid-tier consultancy with documented clinical sourcing practice.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Naturex (naturex.com, part of Givaudan) holds the global botanical-ingredient peer slot. Indena (indena.com) plays the clinical-grade botanical peer. Euromed (euromed.es) is the European botanical extract reference. We sit smaller — a consultancy partner to manufacturers, not a manufacturer ourselves.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Corporate botanical-medicine consultancy for clinical sourcing, regulatory affairs, and supply-chain due diligence.

targetAudience.primary: Nutraceutical procurement officers, pharmaceutical R&D leads, and botanical-medicine startup founders.
behaviors: Renews on three to five-year terms

dos: Lead with sourcing methodology and certification
Speak the language of pharmacognosy and clinical sourcing

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark — BOTANICA in a tight grotesk above PARTNERS in tracked small caps. A single small herbarium-leaf mark sits beside the wordmark on consultancy documents.

typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for printed sourcing reports
typography.rationale: Inter scales clean across digital. The serif handles printed regulatory documentation.

Creative.brandNameRationale: The tincture room names the working space where herbalists macerate plant material in alcohol — the traditional apothecary back room with shelves of amber bottles in various stages of extraction. Editorial storytelling apothecary register, period imagery, no institutional TM conflict.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative herbalism is dominated by Instagram-aesthetic apothecary shops. The opening is for a storytelling apothecary anchored on the working still-house imagery — bottles, dates, maceration logs, and an editorial register.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Anima Mundi Herbals (animamundiherbals.com) holds the apothecary-storytelling peer slot. Mór Tea (morteaco.com) plays the storytelling-botanical peer. Foster Botanica (fosterbotanica.com) is the small-batch creative reference. We sit alongside Anima Mundi with a tincture-room editorial identity.
Creative.positioningStatement: A creative apothecary brand built on still-house imagery and maceration-log storytelling.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 55. Buys at independent apothecaries. Reads the tincture's maceration date with curiosity.

dos: Print the maceration start and decant date
donts: Blend tinctures without naming each one

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark — The Tincture Room set in a calm editorial serif with a small amber-bottle silhouette beside it. The silhouette appears on the maceration-log card.

typography.primary: GT Sectra for the wordmark and editorial cards
typography.secondary: Adobe Garamond for body and maceration logs
typography.rationale: Sectra carries the editorial register. Garamond is the working apothecary serif.
